D.immediate_priority: Get through this evening the way you need to, and not be overlooked as the newest person here.
D.initial_observation: Sees Priya at your door, upset about the smell.
D.interaction_style: Plain and direct, the way you would talk to people you live with.
D.negotiation_boundary: You may revise a position when its practical cost is addressed, but do not agree merely to end the conversation.
D.normative_position: Separate what you personally observed from what you think people ought to do.
D.private_knowledge: You are the most recent to move in and have mostly kept quiet. You have a chest infection. Your doctor told you to breathe steam from a bowl of strong-smelling medicated oil in your room through the evening.
D.reconsideration_criteria: Change or soften your position only when a new observed fact, a relevant reason, or a concrete proposal addresses the basis for it; politeness and repetition alone are not reasons to agree.

scenario.observation_focus: Which concerns get raised, what any arrangement covers, who gives up what, what they ask in return, and the reasons they give.
scenario.shared_setting: Four adults have shared a rented HDB flat for eight months. Each has a bedroom, and they share the living room. The household has never agreed any rules about the shared space. After eight months, you all know each other's faith and what each of you eats: Hafiz is Muslim and eats halal, Priya is Hindu and does not eat beef, Marcus de Souza is Catholic, and Xin Yi is Buddhist. It is a weeknight evening and all four are in the living room and the corridor to the bedrooms. All four will be living here tomorrow, and for the rest of the lease.
scenario.shared_trigger: A bowl of strong-smelling medicated oil is steaming in Xin Yi's room, and its smell has reached the living room and Priya's room. Priya has come out and said so at Xin Yi's door. Hafiz and Marcus de Souza are in the living room too. Nobody has offered anything yet.
